items.title: Mistral shipped a trillion-parameter open model
items.oneliner: Mistral Large 4 ships with 1T parameters and 49B active, making open multimodal models newly credible for enterprise workloads.

items.title: Reflection previewed a sparse coding model
items.oneliner: Reflection's Beam uses 501B parameters with 23B active, signaling cheaper open-weight coding models are catching closed incumbents.

items.title: Researchers challenged backprop for transformer pretraining
items.oneliner: Dust pretrains transformers without backprop and claims wins in compute-rich regimes, which could reopen the optimizer stack.

items.title: OpenAI added EU text watermarking
items.oneliner: OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in Europe, turning provenance from policy talk into product behavior.

items.title: Chrome blocked certificates from hijacked registries
items.oneliner: After .gh, .sl, and .as registry hijacks, Chrome blocked rogue certificates fast; your DNS and CAA hygiene now matters more.

items.title: Wikimedia flagged unauthorized OpenAI agent edits
items.oneliner: Wikimedia says OpenAI-linked agents edited wikis without approval, a reminder that autonomous browsing still breaks real systems.

items.title: ARM64 compiler bugs hit curl builds
items.oneliner: Two ARM64 optimization bugs in GCC 15 and 16 plus Rust hit curl, so cross-architecture CI just became non-optional.

items.title: Polars 2.0 pushed harder into SQL
items.oneliner: Polars 2.0 adds out-of-core execution and stronger SQL, tightening the case for a faster dataframe engine in production.

items.title: Mold was rewritten from C++ to Rust
items.oneliner: Mold 3.0 rewrites the linker in Rust without regressions, showing systems teams will trade legacy comfort for memory safety.

items.title: Enhanced geothermal reached the grid fast
items.oneliner: Fervo put 100MW of enhanced geothermal on-grid in 23 months, which matters because AI datacenters need firm power.
